meta.approval: The user approved Azure Commercial DEV/TEST, self-contained hosting, browser-only plaintext, direct Entra bearer with accepted residual risk, and Bicep in conversation. No deployment is authorized.

inputs.userGoal: Build a research plan using parallel subAgents and scaffold this repo into a MVP Azure Application that leverages the OpenTDF SDK to manage file access inside of Azure storage
subGoals: Private data services and least-privilege runtime identities, with public HTTPS endpoints needed by browsers.
Persistent exportable development KAS keys and origin-specific configuration without a fictitious Key Vault crypto provider.
Two-stage resource-group deployment, no deployment or tenant/subscription modification during scaffolding.
insightsApplied: scope-devtest: resource-group scope, DEV/TEST tags, single-region non-HA baseline, and no live operations.
browser-key-release: explicit origin, tenant-specific bearer validation, claims ERS, distinct role mappings, and container-scoped storage RBAC.
persistent-platform: persistent ACA secret volumes, password-auth PostgreSQL, explicit CA bundle and verify-full, recovery and migration caveats.
endpoint-boundary: foundation-derived stable URLs and a generated second-stage secure parameter file with a nonsecret release suffix so secret-only config changes start a fresh revision.
private-data-and-registry: dedicated delegated subnets, private endpoints/DNS, Premium ACR, and external VNet-connected runner prerequisite.

reasoning.whyChosen: Security and operational coherence: dedicated non-overlapping subnets and a workload-profiles environment; /24 exceeds the /27 minimum.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Fixed isolated DEV CIDRs; check overlap before peering. No egress firewall, VPN, or build agent is provisioned.

properties.postgresInbound: Allow 5432 from Container Apps and PostgreSQL subnets; deny other VNet inbound

reasoning.whyChosen: Reduce lateral access to the private policy database.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Azure-required outbound flows remain allowed. A maintenance client needs reviewed connectivity and an explicit NSG allowance.

reasoning.whyChosen: Operational observability: ACA console/system logs and Blob, PostgreSQL, and registry diagnostics use Azure Monitor.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Public Azure Monitor ingestion/query endpoints with Azure RBAC; no private monitor scope. Log cost, sensitive-field filtering, and end-to-end audit correlation require operator review.

reasoning.whyChosen: Small managed compute boundary with private dependencies and public browser HTTPS ingress.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Single-region non-HA development adaptation, not an upstream production reference architecture.

reasoning.whyChosen: Private image distribution with managed-identity pulls. Premium is required for private endpoints.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Premium standing cost; a VNet-connected Docker build/push runner with DNS and AcrPush is required, but not provisioned.

reasoning.whyChosen: Private ciphertext storage; managed identity replaces shared keys and public blobs.
reasoning.tradeoffs: LRS is not regional DR; versions and soft-deleted data incur cost and are not independent immutable backup.

reasoning.whyChosen: Resolve Blob/ACR private endpoints and delegated-network PostgreSQL correctly.
alternativesConsidered: Incorrect PostgreSQL privatelink zone for delegated subnet
reasoning.tradeoffs: Build/maintenance networks must forward to or link the relevant DNS zones; VNet peering alone does not link private DNS.

reasoning.whyChosen: Private data-plane connectivity from the ACA VNet.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Endpoint/DNS standing cost; PostgreSQL uses subnet delegation, not another endpoint.

reasoning.whyChosen: Durable private policy state with inexpensive development sizing and forced verified TLS from Go/pgx.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Password authentication and dedicated server administrator runtime are explicit DEV exceptions. No HA or regional DR; migration requires schema DDL. Production needs separate migration/runtime roles and measured sizing.

app: Storage Blob Data Contributor at files container

reasoning.whyChosen: No storage account credentials, application client secret, or platform storage access.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Azure RBAC propagation must settle before image pulls/data access. Blob Data Contributor includes delete permission.

secretVolumes: RSA and EC PEM key/certificate pairs
properties.revisionSuffix: Generated nonsecret release identifier, stable when reusing a runtime parameter file

reasoning.whyChosen: Pinned real OpenTDF with claims ERS, exact application-origin CORS, direct Entra bearer, and persistent development keys.
reasoning.tradeoffs: ACA secrets are exportable operational storage, not non-exportable HSM custody. Single revision/replica does not prevent rollout overlap; quiesce old revision before upgrades. HTTPS terminates at ACA; intra-environment transport is protected by platform peer encryption.

reasoning.whyChosen: Same-origin browser UI/API with managed-identity ciphertext access; no KAS private keys or DB password in the app.
reasoning.tradeoffs: Public browser origin and delivered JavaScript remain trusted. Initial sizing and probes do not prove upstream integration or Storage availability.

overallReasoning.summary: Approved self-contained Commercial DEV/TEST baseline. Stage one creates private dependencies and the ACA default domain; stage two uses stable names, an immutable built image, persistent keys, and generated secure runtime configuration.
overallReasoning.tradeoffs: No deployment, live resource inventory, regional SKU/quota check, ARM what-if, image execution, or real-token integration was performed. Checkov is unavailable. Private ACR requires Premium and an external VNet-connected runner. ACA secrets hold exportable keys; PostgreSQL uses password auth and a privileged dedicated DEV login. Single-region LRS/non-HA, seven-day backups, public app/platform and Azure Monitor endpoints, and unrestricted required outbound networking are explicit development tradeoffs. No unused Key Vault, Application Insights, build VM, VPN, firewall, or invented Azure KAS driver is provisioned. No production or accreditation claim is made.
